title: Which Printed Share Governs a Kiosk Trip where the Client also Holds a Site Cafe
content:
Where a client of the Unattended Micro Market Program also holds a contract under the Workplace Cafe Management Program, the standing of that cafe contract and the client subsidy the cafe has met over the trailing year, read from the cafe's own subsidy drawdown entries, can settle which printed share is applied to a kiosk trip.

## Conditions

**Where the client holds a workplace cafe contract standing active, and that cafe has met 18000 USD or more of client subsidy over the twelve months to the day the discount is worked out**, the share of menu price printed against the cafe service model governs both outlets together.

**Where the client holds a workplace cafe contract standing active, and that cafe has met less than 18000 USD of client subsidy over those twelve months**, the share printed against the cafe service model applies less the light-use step of 3 percentage points, the stepped-back share being taken to the nearest hundredth of a percentage point.

**Where neither of those holds** — the client holds no workplace cafe contract, or holds one that does not stand active — no cafe share governs the trip.

## Boundary

The cafe pooling floor is 18000 USD of client subsidy met over the trailing twelve months. A cafe that has met exactly 18000 USD is at or above the floor and takes the first condition; a cafe that has met 17999.99 USD is below it and takes the second.

## Hypothetical readings

A client holding an active Workplace Cafe Management Program contract whose cafe subsidy drawdown entries total 24500 USD over the trailing twelve months takes the share of menu price printed against its cafe service model.

The same client, had those entries totalled 9400 USD, would take that printed cafe share less 3 percentage points; on a cafe share of 15 per cent that is 12 per cent.

A client whose cafe contract stands closed, and a client holding no cafe contract at all, each fall outside both conditions.
